solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Start to generate a little illumination

indicators.note: the start of a word is where it begins

explanation.surface: Someone coaxing a faint glow into life, perhaps striking a match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Start to generate' reads as an instruction to switch something on; it only wants one letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: lamps burning coal gas lit Victorian streets, one historic form of illumination.

clue.text: Feeling angst about embracing hardcore rapper

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold in your arms, so these words hold the answer inside them

blocks.note: the letters run from the last letter of 'Feeling' to the first of 'about'

explanation.surface: A tough rapper whose swagger hides anxiety.
explanation.walkthrough: 'angst about' looks like an anagram of ANGST, but the answer sits whole across three words: G from the end of feeling, then angst, then the A of about.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: gangsta rap is a hardcore hip-hop style, and its performers are called gangstas.

clue.text: Samuel and couple from Bath dance

blocks.note: the usual short form of the name Samuel

explanation.surface: Samuel and his partner from the spa town of Bath take to the dance floor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'couple' looks like two dancers from Bath, an English spa city; it means two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the lively Brazilian carnival dance is one kind of dance.

clue.text: Content to join them, one year, enjoying wealth

blocks.note: the contents of something are in it

explanation.surface: Someone happy to join a group for a year while living in comfort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Content' reads as happy; here it is the noun, what a container holds, which is inside.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: someone in the money has plenty of cash, so is enjoying wealth.

clue.text: African scavengers laugh about hunger strike primarily

blocks.note: a yen is a longing, a hunger

explanation.surface: Laughing hyenas are pictured as scavengers ready to strike when hungry.
explanation.walkthrough: Hyenas are famous for their laughing call, so 'laugh' belongs in the scene as well as in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: spotted and striped hyenas live in Africa and feed largely on carcasses.

clue.text: Just beautiful

blocks.note: the old poetic sense, as in a maiden of the ballads

explanation.walkthrough: 'Just' pretends to be the adverb, as in merely beautiful; it is the adjective meaning even-handed.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonyms both ways: fair means just (a fair ruling) and, in older poetic use, beautiful (fair lady).

clue.text: Country song engages roughly half the population

indicators.note: to engage is to take on or occupy

blocks.note: an aria is an operatic song
men make up about half of any population

explanation.surface: A national song that appeals to about half the country's people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Country song' looks like a single idea, a music genre; the break comes after 'Country'.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: Armenia is a nation in the Caucasus, between Turkey and Azerbaijan.

clue.text: Actual beginning of Mongol Empire

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: The true origins of the Mongol Empire.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'Mongol Empire' as one name; 'Empire' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A loose synonym: a realm is the territory a monarch rules, which an empire also is.

clue.text: It’s unimportant what characterises a vacuum

blocks.note: the everyday phrase for shrugging something off
the physics: a vacuum is space empty of any substance

explanation.walkthrough: The second half is literally true: a vacuum is defined by having nothing in it, and 'matter' is the physicist's word for substance.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom and a literal phrase: 'no matter' shrugs off something unimportant, and in physics a vacuum holds no matter.

clue.text: Initially, Forster may cut novel

indicators.note: initials are the first letters of a name.

blocks.note: E. M. Forster, the novelist, by his initials

explanation.surface: Forster might trim a novel in its early draft.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is Jane Austen's novel, not Forster's, which the surface quietly hopes you will not notice.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: Jane Austen's 1815 novel about a matchmaking heroine.

clue.text: Subsequently going through ordeal with three participants

indicators.note: to go through something is to pass inside it

explanation.surface: Someone later enduring a three-way ordeal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going through ordeal' reads as suffering; it is the placing instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym from Latin: tri- (three) and lateral (sides), so talks with three parties are trilateral.

clue.text: Meagre score in skittles

blocks.note: lean, scanty, as in a thin frame or a frugal meal
felling all the pins with two balls rather than one

explanation.surface: A poor score in a game of skittles.
explanation.walkthrough: Skittles is the British pub game of bowling at pins; the scoring term is actually a good result, not a meagre one.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym plus a sports term: spare means meagre (a spare diet), and in bowling a spare is two balls felling all pins.

clue.text: In the morning, catching companion opening letters?

blocks.note: a crony is a close companion

explanation.surface: Someone opening the post first thing with a friend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'opening letters' pictures the morning mail; the question mark flags that it means initial letters forming a word.
explanation.definitionFit: A cryptic twist: the opening letters of a phrase, like NATO or radar, make up the kind of word asked for.

clue.text: A puzzle mostly concerning part of South America

indicators.note: most of a word is all but its last letter

explanation.surface: A puzzle largely about South American geography.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A puzzle' looks like the crossword itself; the puzzle meant is a maze.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the great river basin and rainforest covering much of northern South America.

clue.text: Okay, state how old you are

blocks.note: to aver is to state firmly

explanation.surface: Someone told it's fine to say how old they are.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Okay' reads as permission; it is the adjective meaning middling, and 'state' is the verb, not a nation.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: an okay performance is an average one, neither good nor bad.

clue.text: Pack animal roughly east of mountain area

indicators.note: in an across clue east is to the right

explanation.surface: A pack animal found somewhere to the east of the mountains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'roughly' seems to hedge the geography; it is the abbreviation for circa.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: alpacas are Andean camelids, related to llamas, that can carry light loads.

clue.text: Two-star novel — no less than that

indicators.note: novel as an adjective means new, so the letters are made into something new

explanation.surface: A reviewer giving a novel two stars, and insisting it deserves no less.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like the book being rated; it is the adjective meaning new.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: 'at worst' names the floor of an estimate, so the result will be no less than that.

clue.text: Run of luck confused skater

explanation.surface: A skater, dazed after a run of good fortune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Run' sits next to a skater and suggests a sprint across the ice; the definition is the whole phrase 'Run of luck'.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a winning streak is an unbroken run of luck.

clue.text: Constantly established high point

blocks.note: the abbreviation est., as in 'est. 1850' on shop signs

explanation.surface: A peak that has always stood firm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'high point' reads as a highlight; it is literal, the world's tallest mountain.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the highest mountain on Earth, and by extension any peak of achievement.

clue.text: Rising trend to accept Conservative decree

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means reading from bottom to top

blocks.note: the tide of opinion is its trend

explanation.surface: A political shift that brings in a Conservative ruling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rising trend' reads as a growing fashion; 'Rising' only turns the word upward.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: an edict is an official decree issued by authority.

clue.text: Cast finished broadcast

indicators.note: something broadcast is heard, so the word is taken by its sound

explanation.surface: The cast of a show has finished its broadcast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cast' reads as the actors; it is the past tense of the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: cast and threw are both past tenses of verbs meaning to fling.

clue.text: Wanders through woods without leader

indicators.note: a word's leader is its first letter, and 'without' removes it

explanation.surface: Someone wandering through woods, leaderless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'woods' must first become a synonym before it loses its head.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to rove is to wander aimlessly.

clue.text: Existential statement has at first mystified prayer leader

indicators.note: to have something is to hold it

blocks.note: 'I am', the simplest statement of existence

explanation.surface: A prayer leader baffled by a philosophical claim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Existential statement' sounds like philosophy; it is just the two words claiming existence, as in 'I think, therefore I am'.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: in a mosque the imam leads the congregation in prayer.

clue.text: Pirate finished after char

explanation.surface: A pirate done for once he'd been burned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'char' can be British slang for tea or a charwoman; here it is the verb, to scorch.
explanation.definitionFit: A descriptive synonym: a pirate roams the seas, so an old word for one is a sea rover.

clue.text: Three attempt taking ecstasy

indicators.note: taking in the sense of taking on board

explanation.surface: Three people trying drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Three' at the start reads as a number of people; it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A specialist word: in cards and dice, the three-spot is called a trey.

clue.text: Range of capabilities initially seen in piece of cookware

blocks.note: a skillet is a frying pan

explanation.surface: Someone showing their range as a cook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Range' tempts you towards the kitchen stove, which suits the cookware; it means scope.
explanation.definitionFit: A modern compound: the set of skills a person has is their range of capabilities.
